newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian net profits slipped 6.7 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Colombian net profits slipped 6.7 pct in 1996.

text.p: The net profits of 167 leading Colombian businesses fell by an average of 6.7 percent in 1996, a report from the Bogota stock exchange said Monday.
It said the figure was based on statistics from the National Securities Registry and that net profits of the 167 firms fell from 606.5 billion pesos in 1995 to 565.7 billion in 1996.
Colombia's economy slowed sharply last year amid the political crisis stemming from charges that President Ernesto Samper used drug money to finance his 1994 election campaign.
A drop in demand, which resulted in a 6.21 percent drop in sales last year, was cited by the Bogota bourse as the leading reason for the resulting decline in net profits.
Despite the drop, it said the 167 businesses included in the study posted an average increase in operating income last year of 15.3 percent and noted that company assets grew by 21.80 percent.
The companies' foreign debt obligations grew by 47 percent in 1996, while peso-denominated debt rose 37 percent.

Despite last year's losses, Bogota stock exchange president Carlos Caballero told Reuters the bourse's IBB index had risen by 27 percent so far this year and said the overall outlook was for positive.
"The outlook is very favorable for growth in stocks," he said.
